content.text:
Found it. This is fixable in the repo, not on Cloudflare's dashboard side. Root cause: the deploy step pins an old Wrangler that enforces the legacy 20,000-file cap.

Cloudflare's static-assets limits are **20,000 files (Free plan) / 100,000 files (Paid plan)** per Worker version — but the note is explicit: *"To use the increased file count limits in Wrangler, you must use version 4.34.0 or higher."* The workflow deploys with `wrangler@3.114.0` (also flagged as deprecated in the log), so even on a Paid plan it's capped at 20,000 — and the build produced exactly 20,000 worker-dist files, tripping the old ceiling the code comments assumed didn't apply (100,000).

content.input: {"filePath": "/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/.github/workflows/docs.yml", "oldString": "          vpx --package wrangler@3.114.0 wrangler deploy --config docs/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc", "newString": "          # Wrangler >= 4.34.0 is required to use the 100,000-file Static Assets limit on Workers\n          # Paid; older Wrangler enforces the legacy 20,000-file cap regardless of account plan.\n          vpx --package wrangler@4 wrangler deploy --config docs/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc"}
content.name: replace_string_in_file

content.text: No other pins to update. One caveat worth confirming with Cloudflare: this fix only works if the account is on the **Workers Paid** plan — Free plan is hard-capped at 20,000 files regardless of Wrangler version, in which case you'd also need to keep growing the R2 offload (more path prefixes moved out of `cf-worker-dist`) or upgrade the plan.

Good — then bumping to `wrangler@4` (≥4.34.0) should resolve it: the 100,000-file limit will apply instead of the legacy 20,000 cap, and your `cf-worker-dist` (~43k files) fits comfortably. That fix is already applied in [docs.yml](.github/workflows/docs.yml#L331).

One thing worth double-checking before the next deploy: `wrangler@4` has breaking changes vs `3.114.0` (config validation is stricter, some deprecated options removed). Let me quickly check your `wrangler.jsonc` and the Worker source for anything that might trip on v4.

This is just a plain Worker (no `wrangler.toml` legacy quirks, no deprecated Miniflare v2 config, standard `assets`/`r2_buckets` bindings) — nothing here relies on Wrangler 3-only behavior, so v4 should deploy it cleanly as-is. The `wrangler@4` bump is the complete fix given you're on the Paid plan.
if we re-run this are alll the uploaded files going to be retained?

Yes. The R2 sync step (`sync-cloudflare-r2.ts`) already ran and succeeded before the failing `wrangler deploy` step — it's idempotent, checking existing object size+MD5 and only uploading diffs, so nothing there is lost or needs re-uploading unnecessarily. And since `wrangler deploy` never completed, no new Worker version was published, so the previous live deployment stays serving traffic untouched. Re-running the workflow after the `wrangler@4` bump will just re-sync any changed R2 objects (fast, mostly no-ops) and retry the Worker Static Assets upload/deploy — no risk of data loss or downtime.

content.text:
No config changes needed. Your `wrangler.jsonc` doesn't use anything v4 removed — no `legacy_assets`, no `node_compat` (you already use `nodejs_compat` compatibility flag), no `usage_model`, and the deploy command already uses `wrangler deploy` (not `publish`). The `assets`/`r2_buckets` bindings are unaffected. The only things v4 changes that could matter to *this* workflow are:

- **`kv`/`r2` CLI subcommands now default to local** — not relevant, you only run `wrangler deploy`.
- **Node.js version** — the runner needs Node ≥18 (already true via `setup-vp`).

So the config is fine as-is; the `wrangler@4` bump alone is the complete fix.

content.text:
That's very likely *expected* here, not a bug in the skip logic. Look at what's in your diff: [known-syntax-issues.json](formats/tokens/known-syntax-issues.json) is part of an "InstUI upgrade" PR touching shared design tokens. Those tokens get baked into shared CSS/JS chunks that virtually every page and demo bundle imports — when a foundational shared module's content changes, Vite/Rollup's content-hash naming cascades: nearly every downstream chunk gets a new hash too, even if its own source is untouched. With ~95k demo/asset files across 44 locales, a token change at the root of that dependency graph can legitimately invalidate almost all of them in one shot.

The skip logic itself (size + MD5 against the R2 listing) is sound — Cloudflare's List Objects API returns the etag as a plain unquoted hex MD5 for non-multipart uploads (confirmed via their API docs), so there's no quoting/format mismatch to worry about.

The real problem is the job hit its `timeout-minutes: 300` wall (the "cancelled ... 5h0m16s" matches exactly) while re-uploading a legitimately huge batch, at only `concurrency: 6`. A few options:

content.input:
{"filePath": "/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/.github/workflows/docs.yml", "oldString": "          CLOUDFLARE_R2_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_R2_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY || '6' }}", "newString": "          # A shared-token change can invalidate content hashes across nearly every asset at once
          # (e.g. an InstUI token bump); 6 concurrent PUTs is too slow to clear ~95k files inside the
          # job's 300-minute cap. The script's existing retry/backoff absorbs any 429s this causes.
          CLOUDFLARE_R2_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_R2_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY || '24' }}"}
content.name: replace_string_in_file

content.text:
Bumped the default R2 upload concurrency from 6 → 24 (in [docs.yml](.github/workflows/docs.yml#L317)) rather than pushing `timeout-minutes` further — it's already at 300, and GitHub-hosted runners hard-cap jobs at 360 minutes regardless, so there's little headroom there anyway.

A few notes:
- Since the sync is resumable (size+MD5 diffed against what's already in R2), re-running now will pick up wherever the timed-out run left off — it won't restart from zero.
- If it still doesn't clear in time, you can raise it further without a code change via the `CLOUDFLARE_R2_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY` **repository variable** (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables), which overrides this fallback.
- This mass-invalidation is a one-time cost of the InstUI token upgrade touching shared chunks; subsequent normal docs pushes should go back to mostly-skip, fast syncs.
